subject: Scaling forecast and hot-standby allocation for Zenith renewal — decision points
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alexr@zenithlabs.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal sizing: projected headroom vs hot-standby ask

Hi Kimberly,

We're finalizing our renewal paperwork and want to confirm sizing approach. Usage in Q3 spiked due to a model test (50% traffic increase for two weeks) and our average GPU utilization across the fleet is now ~78%. Procurement is asking whether the renewal should include an explicit hot-standby buffer (we currently have 10% burst credits).

Can you help with a recommendation for:
- baseline reserved GPUs to cover steady-state (based on our attached export)
- proposed hot-standby count to meet a 99.9% availability target during burst windows
- any operational suggestions to reduce unit cost while keeping headroom (e.g., preemptible buffer, tiered routing, K/V cache tuning)

Attached: Zenith_Sizing_Sheet_v3.xlsx (usage export).

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Senior ML Platform Engineer
Zenith Labs

---
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alexr@zenithlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sizing: projected headroom vs hot-standby ask

Alex —

Thanks for the data. Quick read shows a sustained shift in 95th percentile token rate and a couple of short, high-concurrency windows. Short summary and recommendation below.

Baseline recommendation (steady-state):
- Reserve GPUs: increase baseline reserve by ~12% from current commit to cover new 95th percentile. This maps to +6 A100-equivalent slots for your fleet size.

Hot-standby buffer (targeting 99.9%):
- Recommend explicit hot-standby pool of 4 GPUs (A100 equiv) that can be autoswapped into production for regional spikes.
- Keep existing 10% burst credits for micro-bursts, and configure automatic fallback routing to a lower-cost quantized variant if latency SLOs are missed.

Cost/ops levers to consider:
- Short term: enable prefix KV caching on high-traffic endpoints (likely 10–20% token savings).
- Medium term: set up a preemptible-backed standby pool for non-SLA-critical traffic to reduce reserved cost vs full-on reserved GPUs.
- Add a short canary to measure quantized variant quality before broad rollout.

I'll loop in Ben to align on commercial (pricing for the +6 reserve + 4 hot-standby) and Karthik for operational runway and deployment plan. Can we aim to present a proposal to Procurement by 2027-10-30?

Attachment: Redwood_HotStandby_SLOs.pdf (hot-standby operating playbook)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-25T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal sizing: projected headroom vs hot-standby ask

Team —

Quick commercial sketch for Zenith (ZTH-2027-091):
- Incremental reserved: +6 A100-eq -> list price $X, we can offer a 12% commit discount given multi-year intent (they sign 12-month addendum).
- Hot-standby: 4 A100-eq as a mix of reserved (2) + preemptible standby (2) to balance cost and reliability. Proposed blended rate to client: 30% discount on preemptible portion, 8% on reserved add-on.

Action items for the proposal:
1) Karthik: provide ops SLA matrix and activation runbook for hot-standby switching (include average failover latency and KV cache warm-up time).
2) Marissa: produce a one-pager showing cost delta between pure reserved vs mixed standby over 12 months.
3) Kimberly: finalize commercial terms and send to Procurement by Friday 10/30.

I'll draft pricing lines after Marissa's one-pager.

-ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal sizing: projected headroom vs hot-standby ask

Ben / Kim / Marissa —

Attached runbook + short performance notes: failover latency for an instance swap (cold KV) is typically 18–55s depending on KV warm-up. With a pre-warmed cache (we recommend priming top 20 prompts), median latency drops to ~12s. Key notes:
- Hot-standby activation: automated health check triggers scale-up, and traffic shifts within the second routing window (using our smart routing policy).
- KV cache warm-up plan: 1) prime from top prompts on scheduled pre-warm 5 minutes before expected peak; 2) fall back to quantized variant if latency SLO > threshold after 45s.

Also attached a quick table mapping "+6 reserve +4 standby (mixed)" to expected utilization curves and monthly cost delta. I'll upload the CSV to the deal folder.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference
